newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 24.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on March 24. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Forty-eight East Timorese youths were detained and 11 injured in a protest at the hotel in the East Timor capital Dili where a special envoy of the U.N. Secretary-General was staying while on a familiarisation trip to the territory.
The Indonesian Council of Ulemas has called on Indonesian Moslems as the majority population to help establish peace and national unity and prevent social unrest.

A consortium of two local companies and a foreign enterprise have won government approval to develop a 130 billion ($53.83 million) drinking water project in Sidoarjo, East Java, under a 25-year build-operate-transfer contract.
The mining ministry will check reports that the data on the size of the huge Busang gold find in East Kalimantan has been overstated.
The Indonesian Council of Ulemas has urged Moslems to use their right to vote and not boycott the May general elections.
